description:
## Goal

Compile each fixture/configuration observation once, then fan immutable results into every permanent corpus ratchet that asks the same question. Reduce validation work without weakening non-vacuity, failure attribution, determinism, or configuration isolation.

## Current signal

The combined stack has multiple cross-process and corpus tests that independently compile the same three target fixtures to prove causal work, backend identity, and public-trace bounds. The existing duplicate three-fixture paths perform six compilations where one observation per fixture can serve every pure assertion: 6 -> 3 compiles.

The ignored native corpus already demonstrates the useful model: one deterministic fixture selection and compilation pass supplies semantic population, physical sharing, body/byte, exclusion, and work counters. This ticket generalizes that ownership without moving the expensive ignored corpus into ordinary CI.

## Correct model

- Inventory only byte-for-byte identical fixture + compiler configuration + front-door observations.
- One harness call owns setup, process lifecycle, timeout, output cleanup, and compilation, and returns an immutable typed observation bundle.
- Pure named ratchets consume that bundle; none silently recompiles or mutates it.
- A compile-count oracle proves one production per unique observation key.
- Every ratchet keeps its own explicit non-vacuity checks and diagnostic context. One failure identifies the fixture, door/configuration, producer phase, and exact ratchet.
- Configuration, feature, environment, telemetry subscription, target door, and process-boundary differences remain separate observations.

## TDD

1. Convert the duplicate three-fixture tests and pin exactly three compiles instead of six with identical causal/backend/public results.
2. Deliberately fail each consumer in a harness test and prove attribution remains specific.
3. Preserve expected-fatal, panic, timeout, and filter classifications; no skipped/empty population can satisfy a ratchet.
4. Prove deterministic result order and collision-free temporary/output ownership under parallel tests.

## Required deletion and acceptance

Delete superseded per-ratchet compilation loops, duplicate fixture filters, temporary adapters, and redundant cleanup. Add no global mutable cache and never reuse across distinct configurations. Focused harness/process tests, affected cross-process ratchets, full library/integration tests, formatting, check, and strict clippy pass. The permanent ordinary-CI compile count falls from 6 to 3 for the current duplicate three-fixture coverage.
title: Compile each fixture observation once and fan permanent ratchets over it
